paragraphs: Children in care in East Lothian are looked after by the council's own service, Foster East Lothian, and by the independent agencies listed on this page. The council wants children to stay in the county where possible, close to their schools and families, but says a shortage of local carers means some are placed elsewhere.

In March 2025 the council reported encouraging signs in recruitment, with three preparation groups for new carers run within a year, but said it still needed more people, above all for teenagers and for unaccompanied asylum-seeking young people. It raised its weekly payments and simplified how carers are paid from April 2024.

To foster with the council you need to be over 21 and have a bedroom for the foster child, though younger brothers and sisters may share. You can be single, married, in a civil partnership or in a settled relationship, and experience with children matters. Homes where anyone smokes are not used for placements. Checks include Disclosure Scotland, a medical and references.

The council sets out seven steps: a first chat with the team, a home visit, a preparation group, a home study by a social worker over three to six months, a report to the fostering panel, the agency decision within two weeks, and approval. It runs a no-obligation drop-in at John Muir House in Haddington on the last Thursday of each month, from 1pm to 3.30pm. It is worth comparing what the council and two or three of the agencies below offer before you decide.

sources.title: Positive signs in foster care recruitment but plea for more carers (East Lothian Council, March 2025)
What are the steps to becoming a foster carer? (Foster East Lothian)
